=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer-side review of the Seller's update and Disclosure Letter

I have only the Seller's cover note, key positions and Disclosure Letter. I haven't seen the underlying data room documents (DD-002 to DD-012) or the full SPA draft, so points about what those documents say are the Seller's own characterisations. Verify them against the source documents.

## 1. Threshold point: the "FINAL / market standard" framing

- **The "settled at principal level" claim is unverified.** Confirm with our principals and deal team what was actually agreed, and in what form. Do not treat the statement as binding or as an instruction.
- **The note contradicts itself.** The preamble says all positions are FINAL, but the fundamental/title position, the "all Claims" limitation wording and the tax/IP position are each introduced as things the Seller "proposes". Those are open by the Seller's own wording, and I would treat only the headline numbers (20% cap, AUD 25k de minimis, AUD 250k basket, 18 months) as possibly agreed.
- **The market assertion is self-serving and selective.** Ranges for general warranties may be defensible, but market practice does not support applying them to title, capacity, tax, fraud or specific indemnities. Those are normally capped at price or uncapped, with much longer time limits.
- **The Disclosure Letter undercuts the cover note.** The cover note says Bluefen is "addressed", but the letter says no consent has been included. The letter also says the DD-006 incident is unresolved, while the cover note calls it "not expected to be material". Rely on the letter's admissions.

## 2. Structural issues (the package as a whole)

**a. Limitations applied to everything (cl 12.3/13, 9.3/12.8/20.5).**
Applying the cap, basket, 18-month limit, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses to "all Claims of any nature" is the most dangerous drafting point. As drafted it would:
- cap title and capacity claims at 20% (AUD 4.8m) and cut them off after 18 months, so a defect in title to 100% of the business would be largely unrecoverable;
- sweep in specific indemnities (Ironquay, and anything we add for the incident), tax, and potentially fraud or wilful concealment;
- exclude statutory claims, where the law may limit exclusion in any case (e.g. misleading or deceptive conduct under the ACL/ASIC Act and Corporations Act). A broad non-reliance clause also invites argument and gives us no benefit.

*Push back:* the limitations apply to general warranty claims only. Carve out:
- fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority), capped at 100% of price;
- tax and the tax covenant;
- specific indemnities and price/leakage claims;
- fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment, which are uncapped and have no time limit.

Title and tax limitation periods should be at least 6 years, in line with the NSW contractual limitation period (Limitation Act 1969 (NSW)).

**b. Basket mechanics.** "Only the excess above the basket" is a deductible. We should seek a tipping basket (once AUD 250k is passed, recover from dollar one), plus aggregation of related claims so the AUD 25k de minimis can't be used to fragment a single issue. Basket and de minimis should not apply to fundamental warranties or indemnities.

**c. Cap and time limit for general warranties.** 20% is within an arguable range but is not a given. Given the open data incident, IP chain-of-title and customer concentration, we should open higher (e.g. 30–40%) and ask for at least 24 months so that two audit cycles are covered. Whether to trade here depends on how much of the specific risk we move into indemnities and conditions.

**d. General disclosure (Sch 7, DL 1.1–1.2).** Disclosing the whole data room and all public registers against all warranties would gut the warranty package, and is paired with the knowledge clause below. Reject it. Require disclosure only of specific matters, against specific warranties, with fair detail. The data room cut-off (5pm 22 September 2026) is also now stale, so no disclosure should extend beyond a defined, agreed data room index. Any updates after signing should not cure breaches.

**e. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3).** This is a large problem. It extends to anything our advisers "had knowledge of", including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records. That is constructive knowledge of everything, which in effect nullifies the warranties, because we ran due diligence. Delete it. At most accept actual knowledge of named deal-team individuals, not applying to fundamental warranties, tax or indemnities. Add an express clause that our rights are unaffected by any investigation or knowledge ("pro-sandbagging").

**f. Collectability.** The Seller is a venture holding vehicle that may distribute proceeds to investors. A cap is of little value if there is nobody to pay. Seek a retention or escrow of part of the price, a parent or fund guarantee, or W&I insurance. Known issues are normally excluded from W&I, so it does not replace the specific protections below.

## 3. Specific issues

| Issue | Why it matters | Position to take |
|---|---|---|
| **Bluefen** (~AUD 3.6m, ~30% of FY26 revenue) | No consent exists (DL item 2). "Reasonable endeavours" and "satisfied on delivery of written consent" is loose, because the consent has its own conditions (DD-002, cl 11.3). | Condition precedent for the Buyer's benefit only, waivable only by us. The consent must be unconditional or on terms acceptable to us (no fee, repricing or termination right). Seller bears the cost of any consideration. Add a long-stop date. If we waive, protect with a price retention or adjustment tied to Bluefen revenue. |
| **Riverlark** (~AUD 3.2m) | Under a debt-free/cash-free deal, post-Completion release is inconsistent with the commercial bargain. The facility also has a change-of-control clause (8.1) that Completion could trigger, plus our shares may be secured. | Payout letter before Completion, repayment from the price through the funds flow, and discharge of all security (PPSR, ASIC charges, any share security) at Completion. Include accrued interest and break costs in debt. Check whether the Seller gave a share mortgage. |
| **Closing bonuses** (DD-005, AUD 420k) | These are Company obligations triggered by Completion. Calling them "a matter for the Seller" while leaving them out of the funds flow means the Company, and so we, would bear them. On-costs (superannuation, payroll tax) are unaddressed. | Treat as debt-like or a transaction cost: deduct from the price, with on-costs, or have the Seller fund them at Completion. As a rough guide, on-costs of perhaps AUD 70–75k on indicative rates, to be confirmed by payroll advisers. Review the funds flow and the "Indebtedness" and "Transaction Costs" definitions line by line. |
| **Ironquay IP** (DD-004 cl 7.3; AUD 180k open) | Under cl 7.3, SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. Until then, the Company may not own code it relies on. The Seller's indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment, but the exposure is title to the IP and any claim by Ironquay. DD-010 is not bank-verified, and no receipt or assignment is in the data room. | Make payment and delivery of a signed confirmatory assignment (and moral-rights consents) a condition or Completion deliverable. Broaden the indemnity to any loss from Ironquay's claims to the IP, outside the cap and basket. Run a wider IP chain-of-title check on other contractor-developed code. |
| **DD-006 data incident** (~1,240 personal records) | The Seller calls it "not expected to be material" while its own letter admits it does not know whether anyone accessed the file, the scope, or whether notification is required. At Paperbark's revenue level it is likely subject to the Privacy Act, including the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, which includes a 30-day assessment timeframe. Whether that has already run depends on when the incident occurred, and the Seller has not said. Customer contracts may also require notice. | Request the incident date, logs, forensic findings, the notification assessment and insurer notices. Obtain a specific indemnity (regulatory, notification, claims, customer credits), outside cap, basket and the 18-month limit, with a longer survival period. Seek a retention until the investigation closes. Add a pre-Completion covenant to complete the assessment and notify if required, with our approval of any communications. This is the area where the knowledge and general-disclosure clauses would do the most damage, because the issue is fully "disclosed". |
| **Sandbar renewals** (3 × AUD 110k) | The Seller says "ordinary course", but its own letter doesn't say whether they're unavoidable, terminable, accrued or prepaid. Three identical renewals just below an obvious round number suggest splitting. | Get the contracts, dates, signing authority and any link to the Seller or its affiliates. Confirm whether any were signed under the interim conduct covenants. Treat prepaid or accrued amounts as working capital or debt. Aggregate related contracts for any consent threshold. |
| **Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)** | The Seller says only that the documents do not describe consent as required. That is not a statement that no consent is needed. Check for deemed-assignment-on-change-of-control wording. | Our counsel should read both clauses. Add a warranty that no consent or notice is needed under material contracts except as scheduled, and a covenant to give required notices. |
| **Title** (DD-012) | The share register is the Company's own record, and the Disclosure Letter expressly says we haven't verified title. | Verify via ASIC search and PPSR search against the shares, signed transfers, constitution and any pre-emption rights, and shareholder agreements and options. Check the Seller's authority and approvals. Obtain an unqualified title warranty. |
| **Tax / IP** | "Settled under the general regime" would leave tax and IP exposure under the 20%, 18-month limits. SaaS businesses often have R&D incentive and GST/PAYG/payroll-tax exposures. | A pre-Completion tax indemnity or covenant, longer limits (tax claims should track the ATO amendment periods, with no limit for fraud), and IP warranties on ownership, contractor assignments and open-source use treated at the higher tier. |

## 4. Summary of recommendations

1. **Don't accept "FINAL".** Confirm what the principals agreed; treat title, tax/IP and "all Claims" positions as open.
2. **Limit the caps, basket and time limits to general warranty claims.** Fundamental warranties go to a price cap and 6+ years. Tax and indemnities sit outside the limits. Carve out fraud and wilful concealment.
3. **Replace the deductible with a tipping basket,** with aggregation of related claims.
4. **Negotiate the general cap and period upwards** (e.g. 30–40% and 24 months) as a trade for the specific protections below.
5. **Reject general data-room disclosure.** Use specific, fair disclosure against defined warranties and a fixed data room index. No post-signing updates that cure breaches.
6. **Delete cl 8.3.** Add an express pro-sandbagging clause.
7. **Make Bluefen consent a Buyer-only condition** on acceptable terms, with a long-stop date, or a price protection if we waive.
8. **Require Riverlark payout and full security release at Completion,** funded from the price.
9. **Treat the AUD 420k bonuses and on-costs as price deductions** or Seller-funded, and fix the funds flow and definitions.
10. **Require Ironquay payment and confirmatory assignment pre-Completion,** and widen the IP indemnity beyond the SOW3 payment.
11. **Treat the data incident as a priority diligence item.** Obtain facts, a specific indemnity outside the limits, a retention and pre-Completion covenants.
12. **Investigate the Sandbar renewals,** the lease and the Mossvale clause directly from the source documents.
13. **Verify title independently** and address Seller credit risk with a retention, escrow, guarantee or W&I.
14. **Request a bring-down** of the data room and Disclosure Letter to the signing date, since the current cut-off is 22 September 2026.

Next steps I can help with are a mark-up of the relevant clauses, a diligence request list for the incident, Ironquay and Sandbar items, or a short issues list for the principals.
